name: Pearl Violet
lede: Pearl Violet is ColorHub's English name for Fuji-iro, a soft purple that Japanese tradition names for the wisteria flower, and that the RAL standard independently registered in Germany in 1927.

sections.title: Wisteria, twice named
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Fuji-iro (藤色), "wisteria color," after the hanging purple clusters of the wisteria vine, long favored in Japanese dress and crests [1]. The same hue range was independently registered decades later in Germany as RAL 4011, in 1927, an unrelated coincidence of two naming traditions landing near the same purple [2]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places it in block 223, "moderate purple," about 7.5 units from that block's centre[2]. The library's nearest other named colors are [[dusty-violet]] and [[dusty-violet]], each under 3 units away [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 52, chroma 28, hue 308 degrees, a mid-toned, moderately saturated purple [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in only 4 of 23,781 paintings, a vanishingly small fraction, as photographed [3]. With so few matches our data cannot support claims about painters, companion colors, or role patterns with confidence; the honest finding is that this particular purple is rare across the archive [3]. [[painter:john-singer-sargent|John Singer Sargent]]'s 1913 *Sirmione* is among the handful of matches [3].
